Sataplia Nature Reserve

Dinosaur footprints, a karst cave and a glass viewing platform, nine kilometres from Kutaisi.

Time needed
2 h
From Tbilisi
240 km · 3:30
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
All year
Entry
~20 ₾

Sataplia lies just nine kilometres from Kutaisi and is the oldest protected area in Georgia, granted reserve status back in 1935. The name means place of honey: wild bees nested in the cliff crevices and locals collected honey from them.

The reserve's defining discovery was made in 1933 by the naturalist Petre Chabukiani, who found dinosaur footprints preserved in the rock surface. Around two hundred prints have now been counted, dating to the Cretaceous period roughly 120 million years ago. Both herbivore and predator tracks are present, and the site is now protected under a covered pavilion.

Also on the territory:

  • a karst cave with stalactites, of which about three hundred metres are open to visitors
  • a glass-floored viewing platform cantilevered off the cliff, looking over Kutaisi and the Colchic forest
  • the crater of an extinct volcano and short forest trails
  • life-size dinosaur models, which children reliably enjoy more than the actual footprints

Sataplia operates on a completely different scale from Prometheus Cave — smaller and more modest — but it is interesting precisely because geology, palaeontology and Colchic forest sit together in one compact site. Both fit comfortably into a single day.

Practical advice

The glass platform is difficult for anyone with a fear of heights: the floor is fully transparent with the gorge directly below. Paths are paved but climb steadily; a pushchair is possible, though hard work. The cave is cool, around twenty degrees below the outside temperature in summer, so bring a light jacket. Come in the morning, since groups arrive together around midday. Cafe, toilets and parking are at the entrance, with the nearest ATM in Kutaisi.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Take the E60 from Tbilisi to Kutaisi — 230 km and about three hours twenty. From the city head northwest and cover the last nine kilometres to Sataplia; signposting is clear. The road is paved throughout and entirely comfortable for an economy car. Fuel and ATMs are plentiful in Kutaisi. Prometheus Cave lies in the same direction about fifteen kilometres further on, so combining both on one outing is the obvious plan.
